title: Scalar-valued derived sections and their normalized cup product
statement: Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces represented by their existing small affine etale ringed models [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model], representable spaces [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space], and the unbounded derived module calculus [def-sfb-space-derived-module-calculus]. Let S be a scheme, A a commutative ring, Y a scheme over S with a specified isomorphism Y≅Spec A, and f:X→Y a morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Pullback along each affine chart T→X→Y gives A→O_X(T); these maps commute with every chart restriction and define A→Γ(X,O_X). Define Γ_{X,A}(M)=Hom_{O_X}(O_X,M), with the induced A-action, and G_X=RΓ_{X,A} using the canonical K-injective right derived functor. The functor Γ_{X,A} is additive and has the universal left adjoint p^* (sheafification of T↦O_X(T)⊗_A M); p^* is additive and preserves quasi-isomorphisms of K-flat complexes. Its ordinary tensor comparison is the unique isomorphism p^*(M⊗_A N)≅p^*M⊗_{O_X}p^*N sending the pulled-back pure tensor m⊗n to the tensor of the pulled-back m and n, on every chart; it is natural in both inputs. Tensor and pure sections use [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]. Write Lp^* for its universal K-flat left derived functor. The left and right derivations are absolute for postcomposition with G_X and Lp^*, respectively, so their universal units and counits induce Lp^*⊣G_X. K-flatness and representative tensor models mean [def-pc-kflat-complex] and [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. Define the derived tensor comparison as the unique natural isomorphism Lp^*(K⊗_A^L L)≅Lp^*K⊗_{O_X}^L Lp^*L whose square on every pair of K-flat complexes with flat terms is the signed total of the ordinary pure-section tensor comparison: use the universal derived counit on each complex and the fixed K-flat tensor-model isomorphism on the sheaf side. The pullbacks of these complexes are K-flat. Finally define the canonical cup product G_XK⊗_A^L G_XL→G_X(K⊗_{O_X}^L L) as the adjunct of this derived tensor comparison followed by the tensor of the two counits of Lp^*⊣G_X. All choices here are determined by universal properties or the specified unique representative normalizations.
